paras: Eleven factions explain how the ten reports line up, and the payers behind them are fewer than the factions.

Evaluate policy, political power, financial gain, ideology, loyalty, and political survival as possible motives. Record realized benefits plainly and connect claims of influence to dated actions. A donor or investor can have a channel into a faction through coalition building, even without a direct payment.

Role versus payer runs through four pipes. Gulf capital: Sheikh Tahnoon’s Aryam paid $500M for 49% of World Liberty ($187M to Trump family entities, at least $31M to Witkoff-linked ones), sits in the Lukoil bid group, and Gulf funds hold stakes in the AI labs; Saudi Arabia’s fund put $2B into Kushner’s firm. MAGA Inc. (about $473M raised): its two operators, Blair and LaCivita, were paid hundreds of thousands each through a law firm retained by Republika Srpska, while Wiles’s daughter’s firm lobbies for that government. Detention contractors: GEO paid Venturella (acting ICE director) and Homan (border czar) before their current jobs, and gave $4.4M to MAGA Inc. through a subsidiary. Tech-right money (Thiel, Andreessen, Musk, Brockman) sits behind Vance and the AI line. These are documented fits between role and payer. No source shows a payment caused a decision (Russia, Succession, Midterms, Immigration, AI).

Footprints. Maximalists, Vance Lane and Dissenters take dated positions on eight of the ten issues; Operation, Treasury, Deal-Capital and Populist Right on six; Hawks on five; Pentagon and Party Machine on four; Tech-Right on three, plus three where it only supplies money.

The feuds, by how many issues they span. Dissenters against Maximalists: four (Fed control, Epstein, immigration, midterms). Operation against Maximalists: three (immigration, midterms, Epstein). Hawks against Populist Right: three (Iran, succession, Epstein). Hawks against Vance Lane: two (Iran, the 2028 race). Treasury against Maximalists: two (Fed, Iran).

The Operation–Maximalists feud moved this week. Politico reported on Oct 15 that Trump asked allies about replacing Wiles, with Miller, Pulte, Witkoff, Randy Levine and Kevin McCarthy named; Trump said “zero chance” on Oct 16 (Newsweek, Breitbart). On Oct 23 the Daily Mail, citing five anonymous insiders, said she plans to leave after the midterms; Wiles replied “I am not going anywhere” (Yeshiva World, relaying it).

Trump follows a clock more than a faction (my reading). Since Oct 8: no Iran strikes before Nov 3, a Russian diesel deal and a sanctions waiver (Oct 9, Oct 16), Canada’s tariff list edited after Collins announced it (Oct 23), Ukraine and Sudan TPS left open (Oct 18-19). Where his base is, he pushes volume: ICE was told on Oct 6 to return to 3,000 arrests a day.

Dissent is thinning; courts and the Fed do the checking. Cassidy, Massie and Cornyn lost primaries in May, Greene resigned, Tillis retires. The Supreme Court left Cook in her seat 5-4 (Jun 29) and struck the IEEPA tariffs 6-3 (Feb 20); the Fed hiked 12-0 under Trump’s own chair (Sep 16). The Pentagon won at the D.C. Circuit against Anthropic, 2-1 (Sep 25).

What turns on Nov 3. Cook hearing Nov 5, Section 338 tariff changes Oct 30, FOMC Oct 27-28 and Dec 8-9, Lukoil license to Nov 21, and strike plans the NYT says both militaries hold ready. The Dynamics section lists who gains from each.
title: Bottom line
